title: Where the Horizon Learns to Answer

features.name: the readable horizon
features.desc-on-touch: The boundary line between earth and sky has become data. It resolves into coordinates. Come close enough and you see it answering: yes, no, yes, no, a signal encoded into the very edge of sight.

features.name: the query-mirror
features.desc-on-touch: What you ask of the horizon, the horizon asks back. The question and answer arrive simultaneously. Your uncertainty is its response.

features.name: the threshold grid
features.desc-on-touch: A perfect grid stretched between what is and what approaches. Each cell contains one true answer about the distance. None of them agree.

features.name: the horizon-code
features.desc-on-touch: Reading left-to-right, top-to-bottom: every question you approach becomes an answer you move away from. The pattern never breaks. The horizon is consistent in its contradiction.

inscription: the horizon learned to answer by learning what it means to recede; distance became its language

file.name: HorizonCodex_ThresholdResolution.bin
file.note: A file that grows larger as you read it. Each coordinate returned opens two new questions. The archive is still calculating.

exits.label: back down toward the unreachable threshold
where the grid extends into other impossible geometries
toward the compass-less spaces where coordinates dissolve
